blocks.text: What $1.2 Million Covers in the Abbotsford Townhome Market

parts.t: With a $1.2M ceiling, buyers can access virtually the entire townhome market in Abbotsford. Entry-level two- and three-bedroom townhomes in established 1980s and 1990s complexes across Clearbrook, Central Abbotsford, and McMillan often trade between $525,000 and $680,000. Mid-market three- and four-bedroom townhomes built between 2010 and 2026 in Westerleigh (near Highstreet Shopping Centre and Mount Lehman Road), Old Clayburn, and Whatcom Road typically range from $720,000 to $950,000.

At the upper end of this bracket ($950,000 to $1,200,000), buyers find end-unit hillside townhomes on Eagle Mountain, McKee Peak, and Ledgeview with double side-by-side garages, walk-out basements, fenced yards, and south-facing Mount Baker views, as well as spacious master-on-main rancher townhomes in gated communities.

blocks.text: Comparing Garage Layouts, Amenities, and Strata Rules

parts.t: When touring Abbotsford townhomes under $1.2M, pay close attention to garage configuration (tandem two-car garages vs true double side-by-side garages plus full driveway apron parking, as visitor parking is strictly enforced in many newer complexes). In resort-style communities like Westerleigh on the west side, monthly strata fees include access to Club West (outdoor pool, fitness studio, hockey room, and theatre), whereas smaller self-managed or bare-land strata townhomes in East and Central Abbotsford carry lower monthly fees focused on roofing, siding, and insurance.

blocks.text: 7 Common Questions About Abbotsford Townhomes Under $1.2M

parts.t: Where are most townhomes under $1.2M located in Abbotsford?

The largest townhome concentrations are in Abbotsford West (Westerleigh near Highstreet, Clearbrook, and Blueridge), Abbotsford East (Whatcom Road, Old Clayburn Road, McKee, and Eagle Mountain), and Central Abbotsford (Gladwin Road and UDistrict).
Can I find a townhome with a double side-by-side garage under $1.2M in Abbotsford?

Yes. While narrower three-storey infill townhomes often use tandem garages, many complexes in Eagle Mountain, Whatcom Road, Old Clayburn, Clearbrook, and select phases of Westerleigh offer full double side-by-side garages well under $1.2M.
Are there rancher or master-on-main townhomes in Abbotsford under $1.2M?
Yes. Both age-restricted (55+) and all-ages rancher-style and master-on-main townhomes can be found in Clearbrook, Central Abbotsford near Mill Lake, and McMillan/Old Clayburn in Abbotsford East.
What is the difference between a standard strata townhome and a bare-land strata townhome?

In a standard strata townhome, the strata corporation insures and maintains the exterior roof, siding, and common grounds. In a bare-land strata, you own the lot and maintain your own building exterior and roof while sharing private road and utility costs.
Do Abbotsford townhomes allow dogs and rentals?

Most newer family townhome developments in Abbotsford West, Central Abbotsford, and Whatcom/McKee allow two pets (dogs or cats) and permit long-term rentals under BC's Strata Property Act, though weight or height limits on dogs can still apply in specific bylaws.
Which school catchments serve Abbotsford's major townhome hubs?

West-side townhomes typically feed into Blue Jay or Harry Sayers Elementary, Eugene Reimer Middle, and Rick Hansen Secondary; East-side townhomes feed into Sandy Hill, Margaret Stenersen, or Mountain Elementary, Clayburn Middle, and Robert Bateman Secondary.
